item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 121130
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sat Sep 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula.

Central and Western East Pacific (EP97):
Earlier satellite-derived winds indicate that the surface
circulation associated with an area of low pressure located
several hundred miles southwest of the southwestern coast of Mexico
remains poorly defined. Environmental conditions still appear
conducive for development, however, and a tropical depression is
expected to form during the next couple of days while it moves
generally west-northwestward to westward over the central and
western portions of the eastern Pacific basin. For more
information, including gale warnings, please see the High Seas
Forecast issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure located several hundred miles
southeast of Hilo, Hawaii, is producing disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Development of this system is becoming less likely
while it drifts generally west-northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&

High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.description:

220

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
...NORBERT MOVING WEST-NORTHWESTWARD OVER THE WESTERN EAST
PACIFIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.3N 128.3W
ABOUT 1255 MI...2015 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 1760 MI...2835 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 17.3 North, longitude 128.3 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h).  A turn 
toward the west is forecast on Sunday, and Norbert should continue 
in this direction during the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Only modest strengthening is expected through the weekend.  By 
early next week, a gradual weakening trend is expected to commence, 
and Norbert should degenerate into a post-tropical remnant low 
toward the end of next week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Roberts

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 121434
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
500 AM HST Sat Sep 12 2026
 
This morning's conventional satellite presentation consists of an
amorphous blob of deep convection near the surface center that has
been bursting intermittently during the past several hours.  A 1132
UTC AMSR3 color composite microwave image indicated that the
surface center remains near the southern edge of the convective
mass.  The objective and subjective intensity estimates are
unchanged from 6 hours ago, and the initial intensity is set at 50
kt.

Norbert's initial motion is estimated to be west-northwestward, or 
285/9 kt, and this general motion should continue through the 
weekend.  Afterward, a subtropical ridge to the north of the 
cyclone should steer Norbert in a westward heading through most 
of next week.  There has been a shift toward the north of the 
majority of the skilled models from the previous advisory, which 
has in turn placed the forecast track in increasingly unfavorable 
environmental conditions.  Consequently, the official track 
forecast has been shifted to the right of the previous one and lies 
close to the GDMI ensemble mean and HCCA consensus aid.
 
Although Norbert has been moving over warm oceanic surface
temperatures, marginal moisture content in the low- to mid-levels
and southerly vertical shear have been suppressing the tropical 
cyclone's opportunity to strengthen significantly.  In fact, only 
the HFIP HCCA and the Google DeepMind WeatherNext 2 (GDMI) show 
some strengthening during the short term.  Through the remaining 
forecast period, because of the significant northward adjustment of 
the models, gradual weakening is expected beginning early next week, 
and Norbert should become a post-tropical remnant low early Thursday 
(day 4).  The NHC intensity forecast follows suit and has been 
adjusted downward from the previous forecast beyond the 24 hours. 
 
Norbert's 34-kt wind radii have been expanded in the north
semicircle based on a 0842 UTC OSCAT-3 scatterometer overpass.
